drafts.subject: The layoff news at Daniel's company
drafts.draft: Daniel and Emily, I saw that Daniel's employer is announcing 10% layoffs. Nothing has happened to Daniel's job, and an announcement isn't a decision, so let's take this calmly and prepare together. Your plan already showed that cash is the thin spot: $19,000 covers about 1.4 months of essentials, against a recommended 8 to 9 months. The $18,000 card at 24.9% would also weigh more if income paused. Emily's $120,000 salary is a real anchor. Let's look this week at what a few months on one income would look like, and how your $15,032 a year of free cash flow could build the cushion first.
drafts.voice_script: Hi Daniel and Emily, it's Mohamed. I saw the layoff news at Daniel's company. Nothing has changed yet, so let's prepare calmly. Your cash covers about 1.4 months, so I'd like to look together at what a few months on one income would look like. I'll send you some times.

drafts.subject: The tech drop and your January home purchase
drafts.draft: Michael, you've likely seen the news: Nvidia is down 30% in two weeks and US stocks about 8%. Drops like this happen, and your long-term plan was built to ride them out. The part that matters now is your home purchase in January 2027. It needs $113,300 and you hold $30,000 in cash, so the rest depends on investments that are 73.5% in stocks, with technology about 33% of your stock holdings. Your plan already flagged keeping near-term home money separate from long-term investments. Let's look together this week at where that money sits and confirm the size and timing of the purchase, so a market dip doesn't make the decision for you.
drafts.voice_script: Hi Michael, it's Mohamed. Tech stocks have dropped sharply, and I want to talk about your January home purchase. It needs $113,300 and you hold $30,000 in cash, so let's look this week at where the rest sits, so a dip doesn't decide the timing for you.
drafts.advisor_note: Confirm where the home-purchase money is held today (cash vs brokerage) and whether the January 2027 date is firm. Client profile not available (no MCP); tone inferred from the plan narrative.

drafts.subject: The tech headlines: no action needed, here's why
drafts.draft: Daniel and Emily, a quick note on the tech headlines: Nvidia is down 30% in two weeks and US stocks about 8%. No action is needed from you. Your invested savings are 60.2% in stocks and your retirement is planned for 2044, so there is plenty of time for markets to move through this. Daniel, your profile is Growth and Emily's is Moderate; this drop doesn't change what either of you needs to do. The part of your plan I'd rather we focus on is your cash: $19,000 covers about 1.4 months of essentials. That cushion is what keeps a dip like this from ever forcing a decision, so it's worth a calm conversation when it suits you.
drafts.voice_script: Hi Daniel and Emily, it's Mohamed. You may have seen the tech news. No action is needed: your retirement is years away and your mix is moderate. When it suits you, I'd like to talk about building up your cash cushion, which matters more for you than this drop.
drafts.advisor_note: No action needed on the event itself. Cash reserve is the real topic; consider pairing with the layoffs scenario if it applies. Client profile not available (no MCP); tone inferred from the plan narrative.

drafts.subject: What the tech sell-off means for your portfolio
drafts.draft: Samantha, on the tech sell-off: Nvidia is down 30% in two weeks and US stocks about 8%. Your invested savings are 85.1% in stocks, technology is 30.6% of your stock holdings and 92.6% is in the US, so you'll feel this more than most. Two steadying facts: your $80,000 in cash covers 7.9 months of essentials, and Ethan's $12,500 college payment isn't due until August 2027, so nothing forces a decision today. Your plan already flagged the tech and US concentration and the tax cost of your taxable holdings, about $3,032 a year. This is a good moment to look at both together, starting with the missing cost basis so we know what any change would really cost.
drafts.voice_script: Hi Samantha, it's Mohamed. With tech down this much, your portfolio will show it, since technology is 30.6% of your stock holdings. Your $80,000 cash cushion means nothing is forced today. Let's use this moment to look at the concentration your plan already flagged.

drafts.subject: The tech drop, and a conversation for both of you
drafts.draft: Timothy and Melanie, you may have seen that Nvidia is down 30% in two weeks and US stocks about 8%. With your invested savings at about 81% in stocks, your balances will show it. Your $150,000 in cash isn't affected and covers about 16 months of essentials, so nothing in your plan depends on today's prices. The goal closest to the market is the $600,000 home in 2030, which still has time. Timothy, your profile is Growth; Melanie, yours is Moderate, so a drop like this may feel different to each of you. Your plan already suggested revisiting your mix together, and this is a natural moment for that conversation.
drafts.voice_script: Hi Timothy and Melanie, it's Mohamed. Tech has dropped, and your balances will show it. Your cash cushion is untouched, so nothing urgent changes. Since you each feel risk differently, I'd like to sit down with both of you and agree on a mix you're both comfortable with.
